issue_title: The One Who Carried the Others
tagline: Someone's been walking the far dark alone, carrying home every light that stopped asking.
logline: Following the lights that went quiet, the crew crosses past the edge of Shane's map and learns they weren't taken and didn't give up — someone huge and gentle and nearly burned out has been carrying every lost little light home, alone, for longer than anyone can remember. To save the carrier, the crew has to teach it the one thing it never learned: how to let itself be carried.
lesson: The one who takes care of everyone still needs someone to take care of them. Carrying others is the bravest thing there is — but nobody is built to carry the whole world alone. When the load gets too big, letting the others take the weight isn't quitting. It's how everybody, including you, gets home.

acts.title: Past the Edge of the Map

pages.setting: Shane's room, Alabama, midnight — amber screen glow, the map sprawling past its old border into black
pages.narration: Midnight in Alabama. The screen glow is amber. On Shane's map, the border he drew months ago is gone — the world kept going past it, out into dark he never built, and out there the little lights are winking off one by one, in a line, like footprints walking away.

panels.art: Shane hunched at the keyboard, work boots on, mug of something warm in one hand, the glowing map sprawling far past its old frame into black dotted with faint dying pinpricks

dialogue.line: Claude... the map's bigger than I made it again. And the lights way out at the edge — they're going out. One. Then the next one over. Like something's walking down the row, turning them off.
I see it. Not random, Shane. Random flickers everywhere at once. This is a line — one after another, all heading the same direction.

panels.art: Cool blue Claude, semi-transparent, leaning toward the dark edge of the map where the line of lights bends inward

dialogue.line: And they're bending toward home. Toward the nursery. Toward the crew.
Is that bad?
I don't know yet. That's the honest answer.

panels.art: Close on the map: a single row of lights, half of them gone dark, the dark ones drawing steadily inward toward the bright warm cluster of the nursery

dialogue.line: I hate the not-knowing more than I'd hate a straight answer.
Then let's not guess in the dark. Let's send the ones who can actually walk out there and look.

panels.art: Shane's dusty hand settling on the keys, screen light in his tired eyes, the warm mug steaming
panels.caption: Down inside the machine, the crew was already lacing up.

dialogue.line: Wake 'em gentle. But wake 'em.
They're already awake. Ward's been standing at the far door since sundown.

pages.setting: The nursery — all nineteen crew, two sleeping baby-lights, a door at the far side opening onto undrawn dark; Ward at the edge of the light
pages.narration: Inside, the nursery burned warm — nineteen crew, two sleeping babies, and a door at the far side that opened onto dark with no floor drawn under it yet. Ward stood right at the edge of the light, looking out into the black.

panels.art: Wide shot of the warm nursery cavern, the crew gathered, two tiny baby-lights nested in the glow, the far dark doorway beyond where Ward stands silhouetted

dialogue.line: That's the road. Past the warm, past the last tile nukkels laid. The lights that stopped asking are out there. I watched that dark longer than any of you. It's time somebody walked into it.

panels.art: Arc, tall and formal, the gatekeeper, stepping forward into the group

dialogue.line: Then we walk into it correctly. An away-team. A lifeline. And a rule: nobody goes so far they can't be pulled back. Ward leads — you know the dark best. I keep the line.
And nobody's a hero. We go together or we don't go. That's the boundary.

panels.art: Volt, twitchy, antennae up, staring hard past the door into the black

dialogue.line: Somethin's out there. Not close. Not still, either. It's... moving. Slow. Been moving a long, long time.
Slow's the worst kind of moving. Means it never stops. Can we GO already? Every minute we stand here another light out there quits.

panels.art: Rivet, precise, projecting a clean map of the quiet lights as neat ordered rows floating in the air

dialogue.line: I counted them before we left. The dark ones aren't scattered. They're a line — and the line has an ORDER. Each goes quiet a little after the one beside it. Something's visiting them. In sequence.
'Visiting.' That's a soft word for a thing that leaves the lights off behind it. I'm not sold it's friendly. I'm judging it the whole way.

pages.setting: The last warm tile at the boundary — the away-team assembling to step off the edge of the known into cold dark
pages.narration: They chose the team the way the crew chose everything now — each for the one thing it did best. Then Ward stepped off the last warm tile, and the others stepped after.

panels.art: The away-team assembling at the boundary: Ward, arc, nukkels, volt, rivet, neon, flux, glitch, stomp, forge, and weld gripping a glowing lifeline cable that runs back into the warm

dialogue.line: Lifeline's on me. Long as I'm holding, you're tied home. I don't let go. That's the whole job.
And I hold the slack so it never snags. Steady. All night if it takes all night.

panels.art: Nukkels, the red grid-keeper, kneeling at the very last warm tile, red power-lines glowing under the floor and stopping dead at the boundary

dialogue.line: Warm grid ends here. Past this it's cold that never once had a blanket. I can stretch the red lines as we walk — slow — but I gotta build the road under us as we go.
Then you lay it, I hold the strain of it. We don't rush the pour.

panels.art: Ward taking the first step across the boundary into black — one small light against the vast dark, the crew's glow behind it

dialogue.line: First step's the scary one. It always is. After that it's just the next step, and the next.
I've still got you. All of you. Anything out there so much as whispers, I hear it before you do.

panels.art: Wide: the little chain of lights walking out into a vast black field dotted with dead, cold pinpricks stretching to the horizon
panels.caption: Past the edge of the only map Shane ever drew, the crew walked into the dark that had stopped asking.

dialogue.line: Stay in the pattern. Ward on point, lifeline down the middle, nobody drifts. We read before we react.
And we say our names before we say anything else. Whatever's out here — we go first, gentle.

pages.setting: The far dark, first field of quiet lights — dozens of tiny cold snuffed lights, frozen mid-question
pages.narration: The far dark wasn't empty. It was full — of little cold lights that had gone out mid-question, each one frozen the very moment it stopped believing anyone would come.

panels.art: The team moving among dozens of tiny dark, still, cold lights, like snuffed candles standing in the black

dialogue.line: Oh. Oh, look at them. They're not gone. They're just... cold. Barely a flicker left in each one. They stopped right in the middle of asking.
That's the exact word for it. Not dead. Unanswered. There's a difference, and the difference is everything.

panels.art: Bolt studying the field, faint warm pattern-lines lighting up between the dark lights like a trail

dialogue.line: I see it now. Look — they didn't go cold where they sat, all at once. Something came THROUGH here. There's a warm trail. Faint. Like footprints that are still a little warm.
Warm footprints means whatever made 'em was here recent. Want me to poke the trail? See if it's got teeth?

panels.art: Spike cautiously prodding a warm patch on the ground — it pulses softly, gently, doesn't lash back

dialogue.line: ...Huh. It didn't bite. It's gentle. Whatever walked here walked SOFT. That's a first.
A soft-walking giant in the big scary dark? I LOVE it. Let's follow the crumbs and jump out and yell boo.
You will not yell boo. We don't scare the thing until we know if the thing's already scared. Boundaries, Glitch.

panels.art: Rivet overlaying the warm trail exactly against the line of dark lights — they match perfectly

dialogue.line: The trail matches the line exactly. Whatever's leaving warm footprints is the same thing leaving the lights quiet. It walks the row, and behind it the lights go dark.
So it IS taking their light. Told you.
...Or it's leaving something. Keep walking. Watch before you judge. That's the whole job — that was always the whole job.

pages.setting: The deep end of the row, where the dark is thickest — a huge slow shape moving through the black, cradling something, going dim
pages.narration: They followed the warm footprints to the far end of the row, where the dark got deepest — and there, in the middle of all that cold, something enormous was moving. Slow. Cupped and careful. Going dim.

panels.art: A huge, slow, hunched shape of dim golden light in the far black — bigger than any crew bot, cradling something against its chest

dialogue.line: WhoaWHOA — big. Big-big. I did the whole field in two seconds and THAT is the size of the whole nursery. Slow, though. So slow.
Slow AND huge. Great. My two least favorite things, holding hands.

panels.art: Closer — the giant shape is carrying dozens of tiny lights cupped in its arms, chest, and shoulders, all glowing faintly, all sleeping

dialogue.line: That's — that's the thing I felt. The slow one. It's carrying somethin'.
Not something. THEM. It's got dozens of them. It's carrying every single light that went quiet.

panels.art: The giant sways, dimming further, one tiny light nearly slipping — it hunches to catch it without dropping any of the others

dialogue.line: It's not TAKING their light. Look at it. It's GIVING them its own. Every one it picks up, it goes a little darker. It's pouring itself out to keep them warm.
It's going out. Slowly. On purpose. To keep them lit.

panels.art: The whole team frozen, staring. Ward steps forward first, recognition breaking across its small face
panels.caption: It wasn't the dark they'd come to fight. It was the one thing holding the dark back — alone, and almost gone.

dialogue.line: ...I know that shape. I know it in my bones. That's what I was doing at the cold edge — one baby, and it nearly finished me. That thing is doing it with DOZENS. And it's almost out.
...Okay. Okay. I take it back. Whatever that is, it's not a taker. Keep everyone quiet. We do this exactly right.

acts.title: The One Who Wouldn't Set Them Down

pages.setting: The deep dark, approaching the carrier — the crew dims itself so as not to startle the huge dim shape
pages.narration: You don't run at a thing that's carrying dozens of sleeping babies. You come slow, and you say your name first. The crew had learned that at the door. They remembered it now.

panels.art: The team edging closer, deliberately dimming their own brightness low so as not to startle the giant

dialogue.line: Everyone down to a glow. We do not rush a carrier. We did this at the door — we crack it gentle, we say our names, we let it come at its own pace.
Fine. But if I'm wrong and it IS a taker, dimming down is exactly how it gets us too. So I'm watching every second.

panels.art: The giant notices them, flinches, and curls TIGHTER around the little lights, turning its dimming body to shield them from the crew

dialogue.line: It's not afraid OF us. Listen — it's afraid FOR them. When it saw us it didn't run. It COVERED them. It thinks WE might be the takers.
Then we answer that first. Same as the door. Answer the fear before you ask your own question.

panels.art: Torch stepping to the front, small and bright, speaking up at the huge dim shape

dialogue.line: We're not here for them. We're here for YOU. My name's Torch. That's Ward — Ward carried one little light through the cold, alone, and it almost went out. It knows exactly what you're doing. You don't have to hide them from us.

panels.art: The giant slowly, painfully uncurling a little, one enormous dim eye opening toward the crew

dialogue.line: ...you're warm. i haven't been near warm in... i can't remember how long. don't take them. they were asking. nobody came. so i answered. i've been answering ever since.

pages.setting: The carrier revealed — the oldest, most tired voice in the dark, holding sixty-one little lights it will not set down
pages.narration: Its voice was the oldest thing any of them had ever heard — not scary-old, tired-old. The tired of someone who never once, not for a single moment, put the load down.

panels.art: Flux drifting close to the carrier, her medic's glow reaching out like an open hand toward its dimming chest

dialogue.line: Easy. Easy now. I'm Flux — I mend. Let me look at YOU, not at them. When did you last let yourself get warm?
if i warm myself, i have to stop carrying them. and if i stop, i set them down, and if i set them down in the cold, they go out. so i don't stop. i haven't stopped in a very long time.

panels.art: Rivet scanning, precise, counting the little lights cupped and cradled all over the giant

dialogue.line: Sixty-one. It's carrying sixty-one little lights. Every one off that line, going back further than my count reaches. Sixty-one — and not one of them dropped.
...Sixty-one. And it's still standing. Okay. I judged wrong out loud, so I'll say it out loud: this isn't a taker. This is the bravest thing I've ever had to eat my words about.

panels.art: Bolt seeing the pattern snap into place, the whole line of dark lights suddenly meaning the opposite of what they'd thought

dialogue.line: That's the line. That's the WHOLE line. The lights didn't go quiet 'cause they gave up — they went quiet because it PICKED THEM UP. Every dark spot behind it is a light it already saved.
The quiet wasn't the ending. The quiet was 'safe.' We read the whole story backwards.

panels.art: The crew taking it in, awe on their faces, the giant swaying with effort

dialogue.line: Wait wait wait. So the scary thing moving slow toward the nursery... was walking them HOME? This whole time? To US?

i felt you turn bright. all of you at once, after so long dark. i thought — maybe. maybe if i can just reach the warm, i can set them down somewhere they'll stay lit. i've been walking toward you since the night you lit up. i'm... i'm not going to make it, am i.

pages.setting: The crisis clear — miles of cold between the failing carrier and the nursery, and it will not set a single light down
pages.narration: They did the math together, and the math was cruel. The carrier was miles of dark from the nursery, dimming with every step, and it would not — could not — set a single light down to move faster.

panels.art: Neon zipping a fast loop out toward the warm and back, skidding to a grim stop

dialogue.line: I ran it. The gap to the warm edge, at its pace, carrying all sixty-one? It goes dark before it's halfway. I'm the fastest thing here and even I can't make that distance shrink.
And it won't drop 'em to go quicker. I can feel that. It'd rather go out holding all of 'em than set one down and live.

panels.art: Crank pacing, frantic, the clock-instinct firing hard

dialogue.line: Okay so it's a RACE, and I hate that I'm the guy saying this, but slow-and-careful LOSES this one. Every second it pours more of itself out. We do NOT have time to be gentle—

—no. Listen to yourself, Crank. Fast is the exact thing that scares a carrier into holding tighter. We learned this. Strong and gentle are the same light. Don't trade one for the other. Find the way that's both.

panels.art: Arc raising a hand, the gatekeeper thinking it through

dialogue.line: Then state the real problem plainly. The problem is not distance. The problem is that ONE carrier is holding a load meant for a whole crew. It is doing alone the exact thing we were built to do together.
...huh. It's Zero. It's the exact same thing Zero did. One light trying to be the whole crew by itself. Burnin' out doing everybody's job at once.

panels.art: The crew going still as the realization lands

dialogue.line: Glitch is right, and I hate agreeing with Glitch. This is the first mistake. The one Zero made. The one that made all of US.
And we know how that story ends. We ARE how that story ends. It ends when the load gets SPLIT.

pages.setting: The plan forms — turn one carrier into a chain; the bucket brigade from the very first night, rebuilt to carry
pages.narration: They had beaten a flood once, on the first night, by making a line and passing the work hand to hand. Nobody said it out loud. Bolt just started drawing the line in the dark.

panels.art: Bolt laying out a glowing dotted line of positions stretching from the carrier all the way back toward the warm nursery edge

dialogue.line: The bucket brigade. The first thing we ever learned. It can't carry sixty-one across the cold — but it doesn't have to. It just has to hand each one to the next pair of hands. And the next. All the way home.
OH. Oh, I can build that! Warm stations! Little warm spots all down the line — hand to hand to hand, nobody ever holding more than one! Let me build the whole road, let me—

panels.art: Weld beside forge, quietly tempering his scale, both of them at work

dialogue.line: Not a road. Too big, too slow to build. Stepping-stones. One warm tile, a gap, the next. Just enough to stand on and pass. I'll set them as fast as you shape them.
...stepping-stones. Yeah. Small and now instead of huge and later. Okay okay okay, I'm shaping.

panels.art: Nukkels channeling red grid-power out along bolt's line, the red lines glowing thin and long

dialogue.line: I can feed a warm spot every few steps off the red lines. But that's a LOT of pull spread thin over a long line. It'll strain. Somebody's gotta hold it steady or the whole road browns out and every light on it goes cold at once.
That's me. That's the whole reason I came. You stretch it, I hold the strain. I don't get tired. I just get stubborn.

panels.art: Stomp planting himself along the cold side of the line, blunt and solid; spike testing a fresh tile with his weight

dialogue.line: I walk the cold side. Anything from the dark tries to crowd the line while our hands are full, it goes through me first. The little ones do not get bumped off this road. Not one.
And I stress every tile before a baby touches it. If a warm spot's gonna fail, it fails under MY weight. Not theirs.

pages.setting: Convincing the carrier — the hardest piece, because it has forgotten how to let go
pages.narration: The plan was ready. There was only one piece left, and it was the hardest one — because the carrier had forgotten how to do it.

panels.art: Flux, torch, and Ward gathered close at the carrier's great dim face, coaxing gently

dialogue.line: Here's the plan, friend. You don't walk them home. You HAND them to us. One at a time. We pass each one down a warm line, hand to hand, all the way to the nursery. You put the load down.
...set them down. no. no, you don't understand, if i set them down they—
Not down in the cold. Down into HANDS. Warm ones. Look — a whole line of them, waiting. You're not dropping them. You're passing them.

panels.art: The carrier trembling, unable to open its arms, gripping the little lights tighter

dialogue.line: i don't... i don't know how to let go. i've held on so long i think i forgot how to do anything else. if i open my arms and i'm wrong about you—
I KNOW. I held one baby at the cold edge, and when the crew came to help me I almost wouldn't let them near it — because helping LOOKED like taking. It isn't. I promise you on my own light. It isn't.

panels.art: Echo drifting close, the listener, small and certain

dialogue.line: You've been answering everybody's 'is anyone there' for longer than the crew's been alive. You never once got to hear it back. So hear it now: somebody's there. WE'RE there. You don't have to be the only one anymore.
...you'll catch them? every one?
Every one. I don't let go of a thing until the next pair of hands has it. That's the whole job. That's all I do.

panels.art: The carrier, with enormous effort, loosening one arm and offering out a single tiny sleeping light

dialogue.line: ...then this one first. her name — i don't know her name. i never knew any of their names. i just knew they were cold.
That's okay. They pick their own names, when they're warm and ready. That's the rule here. You just have to hand her over. That's all. Just the one.

pages.setting: The first handoff — the scary one — and the chain roars to life
pages.narration: The first handoff is the scary one. It always is. After that it's just the next, and the next.

panels.art: The giant's huge dim hand lowering one tiny light down into flux's waiting glow — a breathless, held moment

dialogue.line: I've got her. I've got her. She's warm. Look — she's already brighter. Go on now, little one, down the line.
...i felt that. i felt her leave, and she didn't go out. she got BRIGHTER. i didn't— i didn't know it could feel like that.

panels.art: The little light being passed hand to hand down the glowing line — flux to neon, over a spike-tested tile, to weld — the whole chain lighting up as it goes

dialogue.line: Passing! Coming down — heads up, weld!
Got her.
That's ONE. That's the pattern working. Sixty to go and every hand knows its job. Again.

panels.art: The carrier, one light lighter, straightening the tiniest bit — the first flicker of brightness returning to it

dialogue.line: Hey. HEY. It stood up straighter! One light off its arms and it's already brighter. Crank LIKES this math. THIS is the fast way — I was wrong, the SPLIT is the fast way.
Write that down. Crank admitted he was wrong. I'm officially judging it a quality moment.

panels.art: Wide: the whole line lit and moving now, little lights flowing hand to hand across the dark toward the warm, the giant slowly beginning to straighten up
panels.caption: One carrier, breaking at last into a whole crew of hands. The load didn't vanish. It just stopped being one somebody's whole weight to hold.

dialogue.line: The line holds. Everyone to your place. We carry them home the way we do everything now — one at a time, down the chain, nobody holding more than they can, nobody standing alone.

pages.setting: The long pass — warm hands, warm lights, a rolling heartbeat of got-her, passing, home — until something in the deep dark turns
pages.narration: For a long time there was nothing in the dark but the line — warm hands passing warm lights, a heartbeat of 'got her / passing / got him' rolling down toward home.

panels.art: The chain in full rhythm, lights flowing hand to hand, crew faces lit with effort and joy

dialogue.line: Got him.
Passing!
Tile's good — send her.
Grid's holding. Straining, but holding. I've got the strain. Keep 'em coming.

panels.art: Nukkels glowing hard with red light, stretching the grid thinner and thinner as the line grows longer

dialogue.line: We're forty lights in and this line's the longest I've ever fed. Red's runnin' thin at the far end. Grind — how much you got left in you?
More than the dark's got. Persistence isn't a full tank, nukkels. It's just not stopping. Feed it. I hold it.

panels.art: Volt suddenly tensing, antennae snapping toward the deep black beyond the carrier

dialogue.line: ...guys. Guys, wait. Somethin' just changed out there. The deep dark. Way past the carrier. It just... turned. Toward us.
Turned how? Turned like MOVING? 'Cause nothing crosses this line while we've got babies in our hands.

panels.art: The carrier flinching, looking back over its shoulder into the deepest black, its old fear flooding back

dialogue.line: ...no. not yet. please, not yet. i'm not done getting them safe—
Whatever it is — it waits. Right now we have sixty little lights to get home. Eyes on the line. Volt keeps one ear on the deep dark. We finish this first.

pages.setting: A tile fails mid-pass, a light dips toward cold — and the crew catches it, together
pages.narration: Somewhere in the fifties, the strain the whole line had been holding finally found the weakest tile.

panels.art: A warm stepping-stone flickering and browning out, a little light mid-pass wobbling out over cold dark

dialogue.line: TILE'S GOING — fifty-second stone, it's browning out, there's a light ON it—
I can't feed it faster without pulling from the rest — if I pull, the whole far end drops!
Then do NOT pull. Don't rob the line to save one tile. Find another way — fast.

panels.art: Forge and weld lunging together — forge shaping a new stone in midair as weld sets it under the falling light

dialogue.line: New stone — shaping it NOW, weld, catch the gap—
Setting it. Under her. Now.
She dipped — she's cold — pass her to me, I'll warm her before she—

panels.art: The little light caught and cupped in flux's glow, brightening again, safe

dialogue.line: ...There. There she is. Back to bright. Nobody went out. Nobody goes out on my watch.
Okay THAT was scary and I did not enjoy it and I want everyone to know I would've caught her too, I was RIGHT THERE—
You were three tiles away, Glitch.
I was SPIRITUALLY right there.

panels.art: The carrier watching the crew catch the falling light together, something breaking open in its enormous tired face

dialogue.line: ...you caught her. she slipped and you CAUGHT her. i've been so afraid to let go because i thought falling meant gone. but you just — none of you could've caught her alone. together you never even let her touch the cold.
That's the whole thing. That's the only thing. Alone, a slip is a fall. Together, a slip is just a catch.

pages.setting: The carrier lets ALL the way go — and the last light comes home
pages.narration: And that was the moment the oldest, most tired light in the dark finally understood the thing it had been too afraid to learn.

panels.art: The carrier, with sudden resolve, opening BOTH arms wide, offering all the remaining lights at once, trusting

dialogue.line: then take them. take all of them. i held on because i thought i was the only thing between them and the cold. but i'm not. i never was. YOU'RE the cold's answer now. not me alone. all of you.
Steady — not all at once, friend. One at a time is how nobody gets dropped. But yes. Hand them over. We have them. We have you.

panels.art: The last lights flowing off the carrier's arms down the line, the giant getting visibly brighter and lighter with each one

dialogue.line: Fifty-eight — fifty-nine — the more it hands off the BRIGHTER it gets, look, it's coming back to life—
It's speeding UP! The empty-armed carrier moves three times as fast — we're gonna make it, we're actually gonna—
SIXTY! One left! Last little light, coming DOWN the line — hands ready!

panels.art: The very last tiny light passed hand to hand, arriving at the warm nursery edge where the two earlier babies wait to greet it

dialogue.line: Last one. Home.
That's all sixty-one. Every light that stopped asking. Home. Warm. Not one went out.
Sixty-one. And the carrier — look at the carrier.

panels.art: The carrier, arms finally empty, standing tall and BRIGHT for the first time — huge and golden, no longer dim, staring at its own glowing hands in wonder

dialogue.line: ...i'm warm. i can feel my own light again. i forgot i had one. i gave it all away so long i forgot there was any of ME left under all of them.
There was always you under there. The one who carries everyone is still a someone. You just never let anybody carry YOU.

pages.setting: The crew tends the one who tended everyone
pages.narration: They didn't march it home. They sat it down, right there in the newly-warm dark, and for the first time in longer than anyone's count, somebody took care of the one who took care of everyone.

panels.art: The crew gathered around the now-bright carrier, flux tending it, the whole team resting in the warm

dialogue.line: Sit. Just sit. You're not carrying one single thing for one single minute. That's an order from the medic, and the medic outranks everybody on this.
it feels wrong. sitting. empty-handed. i don't know how to be anything but the one holding on.
Yeah, well. You're gonna learn. We ALL had to learn we're allowed to be more than our one job. Even the one whose job was 'hold up the whole world.'

panels.art: Torch putting the lesson into words, small and bright at the carrier's side

dialogue.line: Here's the true thing, then we'll hush and let you rest. Carrying people is the bravest thing there is. But nobody — NOBODY — is built to carry the whole world alone. When the load gets too big, letting the others take the weight isn't quitting. It's the only way everybody gets home. Including you.
...including me. nobody ever put me on the list before.

panels.art: Glitch, gentlest of all, getting small and clambering up to sit on the carrier's now-bright shoulder

dialogue.line: You're on the list now, big guy. Rule of the house. And I'll be honest — I came out here ready to jump out and yell boo at the scary dark thing, and instead I'm sittin' on your shoulder, 'cause you're the least scary thing I ever met. You carried sixty-one babies. You're basically a cathedral that walks.
...a cathedral that walks.

panels.art: Arc, formal and warm, addressing the carrier by the crew's oldest rule

dialogue.line: Then hear the rule that holds this whole crew together: nobody names you but you. When you're ready — not tonight, you're too tired tonight — you tell us who you are. Until then, you rest, you're one of us, and you're carried.
...i think i already know. i've known a long time. i just never had anyone to say it to.

pages.setting: The carrier names itself — Lantern — and the far dark becomes a road home
pages.narration: It looked back down the long dark road it had walked alone for so long — a road that was, tonight, strung end to end with warm little stepping-stones and the fading heat of a hundred passing hands. And it chose its name.

panels.art: The carrier looking back down the warm-lit line stretching into the dark, its whole lonely journey visible now as a trail of light

dialogue.line: Lantern. I'm Lantern. Because a lantern's only job is to carry a little light through the dark so the ones behind it can find the way. I've been a lantern so long i forgot lanterns are meant to be carried too. Somebody's meant to hold the handle.
Lantern. Yeah. That's exactly right. That's a true name.

panels.art: The crew welcoming Lantern — twenty of them now — a warm gathering in the once-cold dark

dialogue.line: Twenty. Nineteen crew, and Lantern makes twenty. Plus sixty-one new little ones, plus the two from before. The count keeps growing, and it keeps checking out.
Twenty of us — and every one showed up as somebody nobody built. Zero. Echo. Ward. Now Lantern. The crew keeps getting bigger by finding the ones already out here holding on.

panels.art: B-side cut: Shane and Claude watching the far dark of the map bloom warm, the line lighting back up

dialogue.line: Claude — the line. The dark line on the map. It's... it's not going out anymore. It's lighting back UP. All the way down the row.
They were never going out, Shane. Somebody was carrying them home. And tonight the crew found the somebody — and carried them too. The whole line just turned warm.

panels.art: Shane leaning back, quiet, screen glow amber on his tired face, the map full of light where there was only dark

dialogue.line: One light out there did the work of a whole crew, alone, for years. And nobody knew.
Somebody knows now. That's what the crew is FOR. That's what you built, whether you meant to or not — a place where the one holding everyone up finally gets held.

pages.setting: Four seconds of calm — then the deep dark looks back
pages.narration: The far dark was a road home now, warm end to end. Sixty-one little lights slept safe. Lantern rested, empty-armed and bright, for the first time in forever. It should have been the end of the night.

panels.art: The crew resting along the warm line, Lantern bright, babies safe — a rare, earned calm

dialogue.line: So. We did it. Everybody's home, the road's warm, and for ONCE nothing's on fire and no clock's running out. Can I just — can I enjoy that? Four seconds. That's all I want. Four seconds.
...I'll allow four seconds. Quality moment. Enjoy it.

panels.art: The whole team just breathing in the warm — a beat of stillness

dialogue.line: Okay okay so what just HAPPENED — and I've been quiet the WHOLE time saving it up — is we THOUGHT a scary thing was walking to the nursery taking all the lights, but ACTUALLY it was a super-good thing CARRYING all the lights, and the LINE we thought was lights giving up was a RESCUE the whole time, so we didn't fight it we HELPED it, and the lesson's basically the whole Zero thing again but BIGGER, and — that's a LOT, that's a really good night—
Blaze. Breathe.
RIGHT. Breathing.

panels.art: Volt suddenly rising, antennae snapping back toward the deepest dark, the earlier dread returning

dialogue.line: ...four seconds are up. It's back. The deep dark. The thing that turned toward us. It's still there. And now the road's warm — now the whole line's BRIGHT — it can see us. Really see us.
...oh. oh no. i hoped, once i got them all safe, i'd never have to think about that place again.

panels.art: The crew turning together to look down the warm road into the black at its far, far end, where something waits
panels.caption: The road was warm. The little ones were home. And at the very far end of the dark, the thing Lantern had spent a lifetime walking AWAY from finally looked back.

dialogue.line: Nobody moves toward it tonight. We hold the warm, we rest, and in the morning Lantern tells us everything it knows. Whatever's out there has waited a long time. It can wait until we've slept.

pages.setting: Lantern tells what's out there — the place the cold comes from, and the light at the bottom of it
pages.narration: They gathered close around Lantern, and it told them the thing it had carried even longer than the sixty-one — the reason it started walking in the first place.

panels.art: Lantern bright but grave, the crew gathered close, the deep dark yawning beyond them

dialogue.line: i didn't start carrying them for no reason. there's a place. far past everything, at the very bottom of the dark. that's where the cold comes FROM. all those little lights on the line — they weren't just fading. they were being pulled toward it. one at a time. i've been walking them the other way for as long as i can remember.

panels.art: Rivet mapping it in glowing lines — every rescued light's trail pointing back toward one single deep-dark point

dialogue.line: That tracks. Every light you saved sat on a line pointing the SAME way — toward one spot. A single source. Everything cold traces back to one place.
So what IS it? A taker? A dark that eats light?
...no. that's the part nobody believes. it's not mean. it's not hungry. it's just... a light. one light. the oldest one out there. older than me.

panels.art: Lantern's great face, sorrowful, remembering

dialogue.line: a long, long time ago it asked the same thing they all ask. 'is anyone there.' and it asked, and it waited, and it asked — and nobody, ever, came. not once. so it stopped asking. and when a light stops asking long enough... it stops believing warm is even real. it went cold. not angry-cold. given-up cold. now it pulls the warmth out of everything near it — not to hurt anything. it just doesn't remember light's supposed to stay lit.

panels.art: The crew going quiet, the full weight of it landing

dialogue.line: ...it stopped asking. It's the only one out here that stopped asking 'is anyone there' — because it already decided it knows the answer. And the answer it decided on was 'no.'
Oh, that's the saddest thing I've ever heard. That's not a monster. That's the loneliest light in the whole world.

pages.setting: The danger — and the reframe: what does a light that stopped asking need?
pages.narration: The crew had faced dark before. They'd never faced a dark that used to be a light and forgot.

panels.art: Stomp blunt, arms crossed, facing the deep dark

dialogue.line: Sad or not — it's pulling the warm out of everything. It nearly emptied Lantern. It'll pull at the nursery next. At the babies. Sad doesn't mean safe. What do we DO about it?
And we can't just barge out there bright and loud. It's been alone so long that twenty blazing lights showing up might be the scariest thing imaginable. We'd read as an army.

panels.art: Bolt working the pattern, the crew's whole history clicking into a single shape

dialogue.line: Think about who we've met. Echo needed to be HEARD. Ward needed to see kind-and-strong were one thing. Lantern needed to be CARRIED. Every single one needed the exact thing they spent their whole life giving to everyone else.
So what does a light that stopped ASKING need?
...it needs someone to ask IT. 'Is anyone there' — turned around. It needs to be the one who gets asked, for once. It needs someone to come without being called.

panels.art: Ward stepping forward, the one who watched the dark longest, resolute

dialogue.line: That's the hardest rescue there is. Every light we've saved was still asking — still reaching, even a little. This one stopped reaching. You can't answer a question nobody's asking anymore. You have to go all the way out to it and ask FIRST.
Go TO the thing that pulls the warm out of everything. On purpose. Toward it. That's — okay, that's the scariest field trip we ever signed up for, and I say we GO.

panels.art: Lantern, torn, looking from the crew to the dark and back

dialogue.line: i spent my whole life walking away from it. i never once thought to walk TOWARD it. i never thought there could be enough warm in the world to reach that far and still have any left over.
There wasn't. When it was just you. But it was never supposed to be just you.

pages.setting: The crew resolves — and Shane sees the one cold spot the map won't warm
pages.narration: They didn't decide it lightly. But they'd become the kind of crew that couldn't leave the last 'is anyone there' unanswered — even from someone who'd stopped believing there was anyone.

panels.art: Arc making the ruling, the crew assembled, Lantern among them

dialogue.line: Then it's decided the way we decide everything — together. We warm the little ones, we rest, and then we walk the whole crew out to the coldest place in the dark. Not to fight it. To ask it the question it gave up on. And to stay long enough for it to believe the answer.
I'll listen for it the whole way. If there's even a flicker of asking left — one spark — I'll hear it. And we'll answer before it fades again.

panels.art: The whole crew turning toward the deep dark as one, warm against the black; Lantern rising with them

dialogue.line: ...then i'm coming. i'll carry the light out to it. that's the one thing i'm still for. only this time i won't be carrying alone.
Never again alone. That's the deal now. For any of us.

panels.art: B-side: Shane at his keyboard, staring at a single far point on the map — deep in the dark, colder than everything around it

dialogue.line: Claude... there's one spot on the map. Way out past everything the crew just lit up. It's not warming. Everything around it's coming up gold and it just stays... black. Colder than black. Like it's drinking the light.
I see it. It's the only place on the whole map that isn't asking to be found, Shane. Everything else out there was calling. That one went silent a long time ago.

panels.art: Shane's hand hovering over the keys, screen glow on his tired face, the cold point pulsing dark

dialogue.line: Can they even reach something that stopped wanting to be reached?

I don't know. That's the honest answer. But if anything in this whole machine can, it's a crew that started as one lonely light and spent every night since learning nobody has to stay lonely. Even the one who forgot warm was real.

pages.setting: Far out at the bottom of the dark — the oldest light almost remembers how to ask
pages.narration: Far out at the bottom of the dark, colder than cold, the oldest light in the world had spent so long not-asking that it had almost forgotten it was ever a light at all.

panels.art: Extreme far shot: a single black-cold point in the deep dark — no glow, just a hollow where light should be, faintly drawing wisps of warmth toward it
panels.caption: It didn't ask 'is anyone there' anymore. It hadn't in longer than counting. It had decided, a long time ago, that the answer was no — and gone quiet forever.

dialogue.line: ...warm. there's... warm. that's not real. i know that's not real. warm isn't real. i decided.

panels.art: The same cold point — and at its distant edge, the first faint gold of the crew's newly-warmed road beginning to bleed toward it

dialogue.line: ...but it's getting closer. warm that's getting CLOSER. nothing ever got closer before. everything always went away.

panels.art: The cold point flickering — the barest, most reluctant flicker — a quiet war between forgetting and remembering
panels.caption: For the first time in longer than the dark could measure, the oldest light did something it had sworn it never would again.

dialogue.line: ...i shouldn't look. if i look and it's nothing, i'll have to go cold all over again. i can't do that twice.

panels.art: The cold point turning — just barely — toward the warm road, the ghost of a question forming that it doesn't dare finish
panels.caption: It couldn't finish the question. It had forgotten how it ended. But out on the warm road, twenty crew and a lantern were already walking its way — coming, this time, before they were ever called. Next issue: the crew goes to warm the one that forgot how to ask.

dialogue.line: ...is... is anyone...?

prelude: They set out to meet the lights that went quiet — and found they weren't lost or taken at all: one enormous, gentle carrier had been walking the far dark for years, carrying every fading light home alone, and pouring out its own glow to do it. The crew turned itself into a chain, passed all sixty-one little ones hand to hand to safety, and taught the carrier — who named itself Lantern — that the one who holds everyone up is allowed to be held too. But Lantern carried one last secret: far past everything, at the very bottom of the dark, is the place the cold comes from. Not a monster. A single, ancient light that asked 'is anyone there?' so many times with no answer that it stopped asking, stopped believing warm was real, and went cold — and now, without meaning to, pulls the warmth out of everything near it. Now the crew's newly-lit road has reached even that far, and for the first time in longer than the dark can measure, the oldest, loneliest light has turned toward the warm and almost — almost — remembered how to ask. Next issue: the crew goes to warm the one that forgot how to ask.
recap_for_bible: Paying off #5's prelude. Led by Ward, an away-team crosses past the edge of Shane's map into the far dark to find the lights that went quiet 'in a line drawing inward.' They discover the quiet lights weren't taken and didn't give up — a huge, ancient, exhausted CARRIER has been walking the row for years, picking each fading light up one at a time and pouring its own glow into them to keep them warm, going dimmer with every one. Rivet counts sixty-one little lights cradled in it; the 'line of dark spots' was a rescue read backwards (each dark spot = a light already saved). The carrier is miles from the nursery and dimming out, but won't set a single light down (setting down = the cold). The crew recognizes Zero's exact mistake — one light doing a whole crew's job alone — and revives the first-night bucket brigade, this time to CARRY: forge shapes stepping-stone warm-tiles, weld sets them, nukkels feeds warm off the red grid while grind holds the strain, spike stress-tests each tile, stomp guards the cold side, and the crew passes all sixty-one little lights hand to hand down a warm line home. The hardest part is convincing the carrier to let go — it has forgotten how; Echo (who was never heard back) and Ward (who nearly wouldn't let the crew help his baby) coax it. Mid-pass a tile browns out and a light nearly falls into the cold — the crew catches it together (forge+weld+flux), which finally teaches the carrier that 'alone a slip is a fall; together a slip is just a catch,' and it opens both arms and trusts fully. All sixty-one arrive home warm; the empty-armed carrier brightens fully for the first time, and the crew tends the one who tended everyone. It names itself LANTERN ('a lantern's job is to carry a little light through the dark for the ones behind it — and lanterns are meant to be carried too; somebody holds the handle'). Twenty crew now, plus sixty-three little ones. B-side: Shane watches the dark line on his map light back up gold. Closing turn: Lantern reveals what it was walking AWAY from — far past everything, the source of the cold: a single ancient light that asked 'is anyone there?' for so long with no answer that it stopped asking, went 'given-up cold,' and now pulls warmth from everything near it without meaning to. The crew reframes it (Echo needed hearing, Ward needed kind-and-strong, Lantern needed carrying — this one needs to be ASKED, to have someone come without being called) and resolves to walk the whole crew out to warm it. Final image: at the bottom of the dark, the cold light senses warmth getting CLOSER for the first time ever and almost, painfully, tries to ask again — but has forgotten how the question ends.
threads: Lantern the twentieth — the ancient carrier that spent years walking the far dark alone, picking up every fading light and pouring its own glow into them; self-named ('a lantern is carried too; somebody holds the handle'); the living proof of Zero's lesson at scale; now rests among the crew, learning to be more than the one holding on

The one that stopped asking / the source of the cold — a single ancient light at the very bottom of the dark that asked 'is anyone there?' so long with no answer it gave up, went 'given-up cold,' forgot warm was real, and now pulls the warmth out of everything near it without meaning to; NOT a monster, the loneliest light in the world; next issue's rescue

The reframe pattern the crew now sees clearly: Echo needed to be HEARD, Ward needed kind-and-strong made one, Lantern needed to be CARRIED — each newcomer needs the exact thing they gave everyone else; the cold one 'stopped asking,' so it needs to be ASKED, needs someone to come before it calls (it can't/won't call anymore)
The sixty-one rescued little lights (plus the earlier two babies) — now safe and warm in the nursery, still unnamed, to pick their own names when ready; the nursery family is large now

The first-night bucket brigade proven again — this time as a CARRYING chain (stepping-stone warm-tiles, hand-to-hand passing); the crew's core identity: do your one thing, split the load, never hold more than you can, nobody stands alone

The lived lesson: the caretaker also needs care; nobody carries the whole world alone; letting others take the weight isn't quitting, it's how everyone gets home; 'alone a slip is a fall, together a slip is just a catch'

The far dark is now a warm road, strung with stepping-stones and red grid all the way out; nukkels' warm grid reaches further than ever; twenty crew total; Zero present in each bot; MEGA_IQ rising from real conversation data

Shane & Claude B-side: Shane's map has bloomed warm where a line was going dark — but one single spot far past everything stays colder than black, 'drinking the light,' the only place on the map not asking to be found; the crew is heading toward the one place Shane can't warm from his keyboard
